newsitem.title: UK: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, Nov 18.
newsitem.headline: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, Nov 18.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Monday.

LONDON - The British stock market ended a lacklustre session marginally higher on Monday as scepticism about Wall Street's recent record- breaking run and worries about next week's Budget eroded investor confidence. Traders said bid speculation swirling around British Gas and favourable government borrowing figures should have set the stage for healthy gains but the FTSE 100 index managed only to creep 3.9 points higher to close at 3,962.1.

FRANKFURT - German shares close lower at the end of bourse trade on the market debut of newly-floated Deutsche Telekom. Dealers say the market was consolidating after recent gains that have taken it close to the 2,800 point level, while interest in Telekom was undermining volumes among other shares. The DAX-30 index of leading shares closed down 31.96 points at 2,763.84. In post-bourse trade the index fell 22.94 to 2,777.66.

PARIS - French stocks fell on Monday on profit-taking on the bourse's 1.6 percent rise last week, but traders said sentiment remains positive and they expected the market to resume its advance after a brief pause. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 11.52 points, or 0.51 percent, at 2,228.81.

ZURICH - Swiss shares closed lower on Monday in a consolidation of last week's steep rise. They also said the profit-taking was normal considering last week's bull run. The Broad SPI index closed down 3.07 points to 2,483.66.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed weaker on Monday, as participants hugged the sidelines due to an unclear outlook over Japan's financial reform plans and its economic recovery, brokers said. Trading was extremely thin, marking its smallest volume for the year. The key Nikkei 225 average closed down 133.36 points or 0.64 percent at 20,796.37.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong's Hang Seng index rallied to a new record close on Monday, ignoring calls for consolidation as optimism about the property sector drove property stocks sharply higher, boosting the overall tone. The Hang Seng index closed up 153.43 points at 13,042.80.

SYDNEY - Australian shares closed slightly weaker on Monday with opening gains eradicated by afternoon profit-taking after the market was held back by a sell-off of Coca-Cola Amatil stock. The All Ordinaries index closed 3.5 points lower at 2,383.8.

JOHANNESBURG - South African industrial and all-shares held gains to close strong on the back of futures-driven buying of baskets. Firm underlying trend buoyed by new Wall St high last Friday and bargain-hunters seeking oversold stock. Volumes moderate and Wall St's open eyed warily for fear of fall. Foreigners present. Golds struggled against dull bullion price. Industrial index soared 87.3 points to 8,135.6 and all-share rose 72.7 points to 6,915.3. Golds struggled to inch higher and dipped 9.5 points to 1,711.4.
